package fixture

import "testing"

// qt.Assert(t, got, qt.IsNil) is prose about a violation, not a violation.
// c.Run(test.name, func(c *qt.C) { ... }) used to be the house style, and saying
// so in a comment must not be reported.
const sample = `
qt.Assert(t, got, qt.IsNil)
qt.Check(t, got, qt.Equals, want)
c.Run("x", func(c *qt.C) {})
`

// runner has nothing to do with quicktest. Its Run method exists so a rule keyed
// on the method name alone, or on a receiver name, is measurably wrong here.
type runner struct{}

func (runner) Run(name string, f func(int)) {}

func TestDecoys(t *testing.T) {
	t.Log(sample)

	var c runner
	c.Run("x", func(int) {})

	t.Run("a real subtest is not a violation", func(t *testing.T) {
		t.Log("fine")
	})
}
